forgeModel: Seven occupied axial hex cells retain seven unique physical metal IDs. Each material has one exact required count of one neighbor material; other counts are informational. Actual outlets select the first target-material neighbor in fixed world order E,SE,SW,W,NW,NE; the mold absorbs and has no outlet. Discrete current-layout heat routing is separate from local counts and is not a temperature simulation. Empty-hand FORGE submission requires every local recipe plus actual heat delivery. Exact pair undo restores assignments without refunding time, errors or lifetime counters; three wrong submissions or the active 90-second deadline end a round.

candidateReadiness.scope: Actually reviewed software-browser candidate using exactly the final bundled assets, before source freeze; separate from final packaged QA and video.

modelTests.scope: Hex adjacency, directed heat, exact instance exchange/undo and input boundary rules plus three fresh public-planner different-material trial/undo/repair wins and three ordinary explicit-FORGE three-error losses. Authored rule examples and synthetic thermal/clock fixtures are distinct from public-planner normal gameplay evidence.
modelTests.scheduling: Ordinary wins use runtime 60 Hz ticks and public observations every five ticks, genuine A/B edges and no state edits. Losses use ordinary navigation and press/release. These are defined legal-input scenarios, not guarantees for arbitrary input timing.

limitations: Enumeration counts distinct physical IDs even when material labels repeat.
Ordinary model sequences use genuine input fields at60Hz without browser wall-clock delays.
Synthetic mathematical, pending-input and last-tick clock fixtures do not represent recorded gameplay.

independentPilotReview.scope: Hand-constructed seven-cell disconnected geometry: two Cu/Fe/Ag triangles and one Cu leaf, with requiredCount=1 for every material. Public observations are independently derived from that synthetic board by the reviewed pure cube/heat oracle. No production model, authored board, reference assignment or model solver is executed. The reviewed public pilot and its own public planner/predictor are executed. These are synthetic observation/input-protocol fixtures, not normal gameplay, footage or device evidence.

sourceArtReview.scope: Final source art; ordinary authored model input states and explicit no-op public-snapshot DOM layout fixtures. Actual runtime menu/play/pick/pause uses original states. No APK/device/video/browser-earned-win claim.

hardware.note: Software Chromium gameplay uses real browser input events. Synthetic mathematical/observer, native-room/phone and source layout fixtures are separately labelled; no physical TV/phone installation or device performance is claimed.
